title: Dietary supplementation with creatine in patients with kidney disease
summary: Creatine is often used as a dietary supplement in strength sports. This study aims to investigate whether creatine supplementation can have a positive effect on the progression of a rare, hereditary kidney disease in which an enzyme involved in creatine metabolism is mutated. Healthy study participants and participants with kidney disease who do not have this enzyme mutation will also take creatine and serve as a control group.
conditions: Other chronic kidney disease, stage unspecified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Inclusion criteria for study participants in groups 1 and 3 (group 1: “Patients with chronic kidney disease”; group 3: “Healthy control subjects”) are additionally age 18–60 years, (relatively) good general health, and normal nutritional status.
• For group 1, “Patients with chronic kidney disease,” a glomerular filtration rate of 20–50 ml/min/1.73 m2 is an additional requirement for inclusion.
• For group 2, “Patients with chronic kidney disease due to aggregate-forming GATM mutations,” the presence of an aggregate-forming GATM mutation is a prerequisite for inclusion.
Exclusion criteria:
• Metabolic disorders
• Liver disease
• Body mass index < 20 or >35
• Muscular or nervous system disorders
• Gastrointestinal disorders
• Heart disease
• Arterial hypertension
• Malignant disorders
• Psychiatric disorders
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
